question: On a distribution system profile, what does the hydraulic grade line show at any point in the system?
correctAnswer: The elevation head plus the pressure head at that point
explanation: The hydraulic grade line sits at the elevation head plus the pressure head, so its height above a point shows the pressure head available there.
options: The elevation head plus the pressure head at that point
The elevation of the pipe centreline only
The maximum daily flow carried by the main
The ground surface elevation along the main
optionA: The elevation head plus the pressure head at that point
optionB: The elevation of the pipe centreline only
optionC: The maximum daily flow carried by the main
optionD: The ground surface elevation along the main

question: A hydrant gauge reading places the hydraulic grade 12 m above the hydrant outlet when no water is flowing. What does the 12 m represent?
correctAnswer: The pressure head available at the hydrant under static conditions
explanation: With no flow there is no friction loss, so the height of the hydraulic grade above the outlet is the static pressure head at that point.
options: The friction loss through the hydrant barrel
The pressure head available at the hydrant under static conditions
The velocity head in the feeding main
The elevation difference to the nearest storage tank

correctAnswer: Friction head loss along the main
explanation: Energy is lost to friction as water moves, so the hydraulic grade falls steadily in the direction of flow.
options: Chlorine decay along the main
A drop in the water temperature
Friction head loss along the main
The accuracy limits of service meters

question: Two service taps sit on the same static hydraulic grade. One tap is 10 m higher in elevation than the other. How does the higher tap's pressure head compare?
correctAnswer: It is 10 m lower than the lower tap
explanation: Both taps share one hydraulic grade, so the extra 10 m of elevation head at the higher tap leaves 10 m less pressure head.

It is exactly the same as the lower tap
It depends only on the diameter of the service pipe

question: A model shows the hydraulic grade at a storage tank falling below the tank's overflow elevation during peak hour demand. What is the most direct interpretation?
correctAnswer: The tank cannot fill while those demand conditions last
explanation: A tank fills only when the hydraulic grade at the tank is above the water level to be reached, so a grade below the overflow means filling cannot occur under those conditions.
options: The tank cannot fill while those demand conditions last
The tank is overflowing during peak demand
The tank outlet residual will rise during peak demand
A distribution pump is cavitating at the tank

question: What is the main purpose of a pressure reducing valve between a high zone and a low zone?
correctAnswer: To hold downstream pressure at a set value below the upstream pressure
explanation: A pressure reducing valve throttles flow so the downstream side is held at its set pressure even when upstream pressure is higher.
options: To raise the pressure in the low zone during peak demand
To hold downstream pressure at a set value below the upstream pressure
To stop all reverse flow between the two zones
To measure the flow passing into the low zone

question: Why does lowering district pressure at night usually reduce leakage more than the same reduction at midday?
correctAnswer: Leakage flow rises with pressure, and at night nearly all system flow in a tight district is leakage
explanation: At night customer demand is at its lowest, so the pressure driven leakage component makes up most of the flow and responds directly to a pressure cut.

Pumps run more efficiently at night
Most leakage is caused by customer meters at night
Chlorine residual is higher at night

correctAnswer: Backsiphonage can draw non-potable water into the drinking water system
explanation: When distribution pressure falls below the pressure on the non-potable side, backflow by backsiphonage can pull contaminants into the potable system through an unprotected cross-connection.

question: Before a newly installed water main is put into service, what is the main purpose of disinfecting it?
correctAnswer: To kill bacteria that entered the pipe during storage, handling, and installation
explanation: New pipe can pick up contamination while it is stored, handled, and laid in the trench. Disinfection destroys that bacteria before the main carries drinking water.
options: To remove air trapped at high points in the new main
To kill bacteria that entered the pipe during storage, handling, and installation
To prove the pipe joints can withstand operating pressure
To coat the inside of the pipe so it will not corrode
optionA: To remove air trapped at high points in the new main
optionB: To kill bacteria that entered the pipe during storage, handling, and installation
optionC: To prove the pipe joints can withstand operating pressure
optionD: To coat the inside of the pipe so it will not corrode
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains.

question: In what order should the main steps for preparing a new main normally be carried out?
correctAnswer: Clean and flush the main, disinfect it, flush again, then take bacteriological samples
explanation: Flushing first removes dirt and debris so the disinfectant can work. The main is then disinfected, flushed again, and sampled before it is trusted in service.
options: Take bacteriological samples, connect the main, then disinfect it in service
Disinfect the main, pressure test it, then backfill the trench without flushing
Clean and flush the main, disinfect it, flush again, then take bacteriological samples
Connect the main to the live system, then flush it through customer taps
optionA: Take bacteriological samples, connect the main, then disinfect it in service
optionB: Disinfect the main, pressure test it, then backfill the trench without flushing
optionC: Clean and flush the main, disinfect it, flush again, then take bacteriological samples
optionD: Connect the main to the live system, then flush it through customer taps
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains.

question: Why is a new main flushed thoroughly before any disinfectant is applied?
correctAnswer: Dirt and debris in the pipe would use up disinfectant and shelter bacteria from it
explanation: Sediment and debris exert a chlorine demand and can shield bacteria from contact with the disinfectant. Cleaning the pipe first lets the disinfection step work as intended.
options: Dirt and debris in the pipe would use up disinfectant and shelter bacteria from it
Flushing raises the pressure in the pipe so the disinfectant spreads faster
Flushing warms the water so the disinfectant reacts more quickly
Dirt in the pipe changes the colour of the disinfectant so the dose can be seen
optionA: Dirt and debris in the pipe would use up disinfectant and shelter bacteria from it
optionB: Flushing raises the pressure in the pipe so the disinfectant spreads faster
optionC: Flushing warms the water so the disinfectant reacts more quickly
optionD: Dirt in the pipe changes the colour of the disinfectant so the dose can be seen
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains.

question: A crew is about to connect a disinfected new main to the live system. What result must be in hand before the connection is made?
correctAnswer: Satisfactory bacteriological sample results from the new main
explanation: Bacteriological sampling confirms the disinfection worked. Connecting before satisfactory results are known could introduce contamination into the live system.
options: A completed pressure test report from the pipe manufacturer
Written approval from every customer on the street
A full week of normal water use through the new main
Satisfactory bacteriological sample results from the new main
optionA: A completed pressure test report from the pipe manufacturer
optionB: Written approval from every customer on the street
optionC: A full week of normal water use through the new main
optionD: Satisfactory bacteriological sample results from the new main
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains.

question: During installation of a new main, the open end of a pipe left overnight should be protected in which way?
correctAnswer: It should be capped or sealed so trench water, soil, and animals cannot enter
explanation: Open pipe ends are a direct entry point for contamination. Sealing them whenever work stops keeps trench water, soil, and animals out of the pipe interior.
options: It should be left open so the pipe can dry out completely
It should be filled with trench water to keep it from floating
It should be capped or sealed so trench water, soil, and animals cannot enter
It should be covered only with loose excavated soil
optionA: It should be left open so the pipe can dry out completely
optionB: It should be filled with trench water to keep it from floating
optionC: It should be capped or sealed so trench water, soil, and animals cannot enter
optionD: It should be covered only with loose excavated soil
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Disinfection of New Mains.

question: What does internal corrosion of a metal water main most commonly do over time?
correctAnswer: It builds up rough deposits that reduce the pipe carrying capacity and can discolour the water
explanation: Corrosion products form tubercles on the pipe wall. The roughness reduces capacity and the deposits can release discoloured water when flows change.
options: It builds up rough deposits that reduce the pipe carrying capacity and can discolour the water
It makes the pipe smoother so flows increase year after year
It raises the chlorine residual at the far ends of the system
It seals every small leak so break records improve steadily
optionA: It builds up rough deposits that reduce the pipe carrying capacity and can discolour the water
optionB: It makes the pipe smoother so flows increase year after year
optionC: It raises the chlorine residual at the far ends of the system
optionD: It seals every small leak so break records improve steadily
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness.

question: Red water complaints from customers are most often a sign of which condition?
correctAnswer: Corrosion of iron pipe releasing iron particles into the water
explanation: Red or rusty water usually comes from iron corrosion products disturbed in iron mains. It is an aesthetic and corrosion signal rather than a dosing problem at the plant.
options: Excess chlorine added at the treatment plant
Air trapped at a high point in the main
A meter that is registering more water than passes through it
Corrosion of iron pipe releasing iron particles into the water
optionA: Excess chlorine added at the treatment plant
optionB: Air trapped at a high point in the main
optionC: A meter that is registering more water than passes through it
optionD: Corrosion of iron pipe releasing iron particles into the water
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness.

question: Which pair of water characteristics is most often adjusted to make treated water less corrosive?
correctAnswer: pH and alkalinity
explanation: Raising and stabilising pH and alkalinity helps water form a protective scale instead of attacking metal pipe and plumbing. Temperature and turbidity control do not serve that purpose.
options: Temperature and turbidity
pH and alkalinity
Colour and hardness alone, with no other change
Chlorine residual and flow velocity
optionA: Temperature and turbidity
optionB: pH and alkalinity
optionC: Colour and hardness alone, with no other change
optionD: Chlorine residual and flow velocity
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness.

question: When two very different metals are joined directly in a service line, what corrosion risk increases?
correctAnswer: Galvanic corrosion, where one metal corrodes faster because of the contact with the other
explanation: Direct contact between dissimilar metals sets up a galvanic cell in the water. One metal becomes the anode and corrodes preferentially, so suitable fittings or separation are used.
options: Galvanic corrosion, where one metal corrodes faster because of the contact with the other
The joint becomes stronger and both metals stop corroding
Only external corrosion of the pipe in the soil
No risk changes, because both metals are underground
optionA: Galvanic corrosion, where one metal corrodes faster because of the contact with the other
optionB: The joint becomes stronger and both metals stop corroding
optionC: Only external corrosion of the pipe in the soil
optionD: No risk changes, because both metals are underground
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness.

question: A lead service line is being replaced. Why is replacing only part of the lead line, leaving some lead in place, a concern?
correctAnswer: A partial replacement can disturb the remaining lead pipe and can increase lead release at the tap
explanation: Disturbing lead pipe and joining it to a different metal can raise lead levels at the tap for a time. Full replacement avoids leaving a lead source in the service line.
options: A partial replacement makes the water pressure too high for the building
The new section will always leak at the joint with the old section
Leaving any old pipe in place makes the meter stop working
A partial replacement can disturb the remaining lead pipe and can increase lead release at the tap
optionA: A partial replacement makes the water pressure too high for the building
optionB: The new section will always leak at the joint with the old section
optionC: Leaving any old pipe in place makes the meter stop working
optionD: A partial replacement can disturb the remaining lead pipe and can increase lead release at the tap
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Corrosion in Distribution Awareness.

question: A pump at a booster station trips on a power failure and flow stops suddenly. What pressure event should the operator expect in the discharge main?
correctAnswer: A pressure surge that travels through the main, followed by a low pressure wave
explanation: Suddenly stopping moving water creates a transient: a high pressure wave travels away from the pump and a low pressure wave follows. Both can damage pipe and allow intrusion if the low wave drops pressure far enough.
options: A slow, even fall in pressure that settles within a few minutes
A pressure surge that travels through the main, followed by a low pressure wave
No pressure change, because check valves absorb all movement
A permanent rise in static pressure throughout the zone
optionA: A slow, even fall in pressure that settles within a few minutes
optionB: A pressure surge that travels through the main, followed by a low pressure wave
optionC: No pressure change, because check valves absorb all movement
optionD: A permanent rise in static pressure throughout the zone
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness.

question: Which operating action is most likely to cause a damaging pressure transient in a distribution main?
correctAnswer: Closing a large valve very quickly against a high flow
explanation: A fast valve closure stops the water column abruptly and converts its momentum into a pressure spike. Slow, controlled operation lets the column slow down gradually.
options: Opening a hydrant slowly to flush a dead end street
Reading zone pressures at the same time each morning
Closing a large valve very quickly against a high flow
Lowering a tank level gradually over several hours
optionA: Opening a hydrant slowly to flush a dead end street
optionB: Reading zone pressures at the same time each morning
optionC: Closing a large valve very quickly against a high flow
optionD: Lowering a tank level gradually over several hours
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness.

question: Why is a brief period of negative pressure during a transient a public health concern, even if no main breaks?
correctAnswer: Contaminated groundwater can be drawn into the pipe through leaks and joints while pressure is below the surrounding pressure
explanation: When internal pressure falls below the pressure outside the pipe, water and soil moisture around leaks and joints can be pulled inward. That intrusion path is why low pressure transients are taken seriously.
options: Negative pressure makes the water meters run backwards permanently
It removes the protective scale from the pipe wall instantly
It causes chlorine to form a gas that escapes at hydrants
Contaminated groundwater can be drawn into the pipe through leaks and joints while pressure is below the surrounding pressure
optionA: Negative pressure makes the water meters run backwards permanently
optionB: It removes the protective scale from the pipe wall instantly
optionC: It causes chlorine to form a gas that escapes at hydrants
optionD: Contaminated groundwater can be drawn into the pipe through leaks and joints while pressure is below the surrounding pressure
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness.

question: An air valve at a high point is found seized shut during a transient investigation. Why does that finding matter?
correctAnswer: Trapped air at the high point can worsen surge behaviour and reduce the effective flow area of the main
explanation: Air pockets compress and expand during transients and can amplify pressure swings when they move or collapse. Working air valves release air at filling and admit it during draining or low pressure events.
options: A seized air valve only affects the paint condition of the chamber
Trapped air at the high point can worsen surge behaviour and reduce the effective flow area of the main
Air in a main always protects the pipe from every surge
The valve position changes the chemical dose applied at the plant
optionA: A seized air valve only affects the paint condition of the chamber
optionB: Trapped air at the high point can worsen surge behaviour and reduce the effective flow area of the main
optionC: Air in a main always protects the pipe from every surge
optionD: The valve position changes the chemical dose applied at the plant
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness.

question: Which measure is a recognised way to reduce surge pressures at a pumping station?
correctAnswer: Fitting surge relief or surge anticipating equipment that opens to release the pressure wave
explanation: Surge relief equipment gives the pressure wave somewhere to go, limiting the peak reached in the main. Faster closures and sudden stops make transients worse, not better.
options: Removing all check valves from the discharge piping
Running every pump at full speed before any shutdown
Fitting surge relief or surge anticipating equipment that opens to release the pressure wave
Closing the station isolation valves faster during a power failure
optionA: Removing all check valves from the discharge piping
optionB: Running every pump at full speed before any shutdown
optionC: Fitting surge relief or surge anticipating equipment that opens to release the pressure wave
optionD: Closing the station isolation valves faster during a power failure
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure Transient Awareness.

question: Under Ontario Regulation 170/03, when a drinking water system gets an adverse water quality test result, what must happen?
correctAnswer: The result must be reported to the Ministry and the local health unit, and corrective action must be taken
explanation: Adverse results trigger a duty to notify the Spills Action Centre and the medical officer of health and to carry out the required corrective action. Waiting or quietly resampling does not meet that duty.
options: The result must be reported to the Ministry and the local health unit, and corrective action must be taken
The result is filed with the monthly records and reviewed at the next staff meeting
The sample is simply retaken the following week with no notification
The operator waits to see whether the next routine sample is also adverse before acting
optionA: The result must be reported to the Ministry and the local health unit, and corrective action must be taken
optionB: The result is filed with the monthly records and reviewed at the next staff meeting
optionC: The sample is simply retaken the following week with no notification
optionD: The operator waits to see whether the next routine sample is also adverse before acting
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Regulation 170/03 Class 2 Duties.

question: What is the role of the overall responsible operator in a Class 2 distribution system?
correctAnswer: To have overall operational responsibility for the system and to make sure certified operators direct its operation
explanation: The overall responsible operator carries overall responsibility for operation and ensures the system is operated by appropriately certified operators. Sampling and budgets are separate duties held elsewhere.
options: To personally take every sample collected in the system
To have overall operational responsibility for the system and to make sure certified operators direct its operation
To approve the municipal budget for the water department
To inspect every private plumbing system connected to the mains
optionA: To personally take every sample collected in the system
optionB: To have overall operational responsibility for the system and to make sure certified operators direct its operation
optionC: To approve the municipal budget for the water department
optionD: To inspect every private plumbing system connected to the mains

question: Why does Regulation 170/03 require operating records and sampling records to be kept and made available?
correctAnswer: So the system's compliance and operating history can be checked by inspectors, auditors, and the public as the regulation provides
explanation: Records are the evidence that required sampling, testing, and operational checks actually happened. Inspectors rely on them during inspections and investigations.
options: So operators can reconstruct their overtime hours at year end
Only to settle billing disputes with large water users
Records are kept purely as a training aid for new staff
So the system's compliance and operating history can be checked by inspectors, auditors, and the public as the regulation provides
optionA: So operators can reconstruct their overtime hours at year end
optionB: Only to settle billing disputes with large water users
optionC: Records are kept purely as a training aid for new staff
optionD: So the system's compliance and operating history can be checked by inspectors, auditors, and the public as the regulation provides
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Regulation 170/03 Class 2 Duties.

question: An operator in charge is on duty when a watermain break leaves part of a zone without water. Which responsibility falls to that operator under the Ontario framework?
correctAnswer: Directing the operational response and making sure the required notifications and records for the event are completed
explanation: The operator in charge directs operations during the shift, including emergency response, notifications, and documentation. Compensation and purchasing decisions sit outside that role.
options: Directing the operational response and making sure the required notifications and records for the event are completed
Deciding whether the municipality will compensate customers for the outage
Approving the contractor invoice before any repair work can start
Rewriting the system's sampling schedule to skip the affected area

optionB: Deciding whether the municipality will compensate customers for the outage
optionC: Approving the contractor invoice before any repair work can start
optionD: Rewriting the system's sampling schedule to skip the affected area
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Regulation 170/03 Class 2 Duties.

question: A Class 2 operator is asked to perform a duty that is normally done at a higher classification level with no qualified operator available. What is the correct approach?
correctAnswer: Escalate to the overall responsible operator so a properly certified operator directs the work
explanation: Ontario's certification framework ties duties to certified operators. Escalating protects both the public and the operator, while falsifying or hiding records creates a far more serious problem.
options: Do the work quietly and record another operator's name in the log
Skip the duty and leave no record that it was missed
Escalate to the overall responsible operator so a properly certified operator directs the work
Ask a contractor on site to sign the operating log instead
optionA: Do the work quietly and record another operator's name in the log
optionB: Skip the duty and leave no record that it was missed

sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Regulation 170/03 Class 2 Duties.

question: Several taste and odour complaints arrive on the same morning from one street, while the rest of the zone reports nothing. What is the best first interpretation?
correctAnswer: A localised cause near that street is more likely than a plant wide problem, so the investigation should start locally
explanation: A tight cluster in space and time points to a local cause such as a recent repair, a dead end, or a cross connection nearby. Plant wide causes usually produce complaints spread across the system.
options: A localised cause near that street is more likely than a plant wide problem, so the investigation should start locally
The treatment plant process has failed and the whole system is affected
The complaints can be closed, because one street is too small to matter
Customers on that street must all have plumbing faults at the same time

question: During a low pressure complaint investigation, the operator finds normal pressure at the hydrant on the street but low pressure inside the building. What does that pattern suggest?
correctAnswer: The problem is likely in the service line or the building plumbing, not in the distribution main
explanation: Good street pressure with poor building pressure moves the search downstream of the main: a partly closed curb stop, a blocked service, or an internal plumbing restriction. Zone wide action is not supported by that evidence.

The whole pressure zone needs to be flushed before anything else is checked

question: After a complaint investigation finds a low chlorine residual and stagnant water at a dead end, what follow up closes the loop properly?
correctAnswer: Flush or otherwise correct the condition, resample to confirm recovery, and record the outcome for the customer file
explanation: Finding a cause is only half the work. Correcting it, confirming with a resample, and documenting the result shows the complaint was actually resolved.
options: Tell the customer the water always looks that way in summer
Flush or otherwise correct the condition, resample to confirm recovery, and record the outcome for the customer file
Close the complaint because a cause was identified, with no further check
Wait for the customer to complain a second time before sampling

question: Complaint records for a subdivision show the same earthy odour complaint every late summer for three years. How should a Class 2 operator use that history?

Respond to each year as a surprise with no change in practice

Assume the customers are coordinating their complaints

correctAnswer: Defects in materials, joints, and bedding are easy to correct then and hidden once the trench is filled

The trench must stay open until the customer moves in

question: As part of a service connection program, why are records kept of service line material on both the municipal and private sides of a property?

question: A new commercial service is being planned for a building with a boiler feed and a chemical mixing tank. What should the service connection review flag?

question: Two cells of a reservoir are available, but demand is low for an extended period. What operating strategy best protects water quality?
